discovery_and_supplementary_preview_rule: For G at each cutoff independently choose earliest predicted destination arrival after fixed access. Keep cases with eligible endpoint labels and >=300s arrival/departure forecast miss. For F the 30-minute processed arrival horizon truncates the complete catchable route; discover supplementary origin-only cases using the earliest catchable F09S departure with an eligible label and >=300s departure miss. Per route/day select at most4 distinct trips in chronological order, >=60min apart. No model output or alternative outcome is inspected. Raw replay rechecks complete forecasts, labels and the cross-route baseline winner.
limitations: Case discovery is retrospective and conditioned on later forecast errors, not an online delay detector.
The initial candidate pool comes from the scoped zero-to-thirty-minute historical features; extracted raw snapshots retain all original trip forecasts.
Fixed supplied paths and authored walking assumptions do not establish historical route-provider output or walking observations.
Content-deduplicated historical alerts do not establish a fresh unchanged alert fetch.
Final-prediction CSV outcomes are proxies, not observed passenger outcomes; missing or missed-boarding outcomes must remain unavailable.

selection_rule: Use every retrospectively discovered qualifying cutoff for raw screening, before per-route limits, distinct-train filtering, or episode spacing. The scout's at-most-four per-route/day shortlist is a supplementary preview only and is not the replay input. The separate evaluator uses complete raw forecasts to choose the same-cutoff fastest unmodified-MTA supplied path, tests its destination proxy error, then selects chronological distinct-train episodes. Model outputs and alternative outcome advantages must not enter case selection.
